My best advice:

  • Create a secondary subverse and use it as a "development environment" to play around in... just don't forget that your test posts will appear on /v/All;

  • Use FireFox as your development browser and right-click on the element you want to customize and select "Inspect Element" from the pop-up menu. This will allow you to explore the element tree and make real-time changes - which really helps during the learning process. Most browsers have a similar feature but I find FireFox's to be the best.

  • Don't bother with CSS editing software, just click on "Edit Stylesheet" and use the standard Voat text editor;

  • I recommend installing FireFox, Chrome, IE, Safari and Opera browsers so you can regularly do cross-browser testing;

  • If your editing a stylesheet for a sub with a lot of users, don't underestimate how many people you'll piss off if your changes aren't customized to the different device types of Smartphone, Tablet and PC. It's really easy and really lazy to ignore Smartphone users if you don't use a Smartphone often, however your users will curb-stomp you if your design isn't functional on itsy-bitsy-teeniet-weenie screens.
